name: François Mitterrand
role: President of France (1981–1995); first Socialist President of the Fifth Republic
summary: Mitterrand led the French Socialist Party to power in 1981 and presided over nationalisations, decentralisation, the abolition of the death penalty and an independent audiovisual authority, while defending the nuclear deterrent, the presidential office and a federalising European single market. He campaigned for pluralism, a wealth tax and a minimum income, and for the droit du sol.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He defended social security as instrument of liberty removed from the law of money, with contributions by means and benefits by need, and rejected health care by market with medicine for the rich and for the poor.

public-ownership.rationale: He defended the 1981 nationalisations as a success that saved firms bled by their private owners, regretted not creating a public machine-tool sector, and said he would stop the nationalisation-privatisation 'ballet'.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He announced the return of the wealth tax on the richest 100,000 to finance the minimum income, saying those who have much should help those who have nothing.

unions-good.rationale: He wrote that modern social relations suppose recognition of the trade-union fact by all and welcomed the Auroux laws of 1982.

decide-locally.rationale: He called decentralisation the master work of his first term, to diffuse direct responsibility wherever people live and work, which gives liberty its real content.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He said the United Nations is coming into its own as a judge defining and implementing the law and that France implements Security Council resolutions and embargoes.

nation-first.rationale: He warned against looking inwards and affirming one's identity through xenophobia or nationalism, and called interdependence of destinies a fact for all.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He said nationalised firms reshaped sectors in crisis and served as a spearhead, and regretted that no strong public machine-tool sector was created from public capital.

one-party-rule.rationale: He said he would advance on the road of pluralism, the confrontation of differences with respect for others, and a new alliance of socialism and liberty.

democracy-best.rationale: He hailed democracy's advance in 1989 and said freedom to speak, to elect one's leaders, equality and respect for human rights are values nearly universally agreed on.

direct-votes.rationale: He said he still wished referendums on major problems of society, under a Constitutional Council check, and wanted study of a popular-initiative referendum.

war-builds-character.rationale: He said peoples hate war having suffered it and described victories as ephemeral, leaving the victor to build on blood and the vanquished to dream of revenge.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He said Israel has the right to exist within safe and recognised borders and that the Palestinian people are entitled to aspire to a homeland.

national-self-determination.rationale: He called the self-determination of peoples a principle which brooks no exception and said peoples threatened with losing it deserve more intransigence.

class-collaboration.rationale: He called for social dialogue and mutual understanding between employers and unions through the Auroux laws and said the 1981 majority aimed to rally all the French, appealing for national consent beyond doctrinal preferences.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He named freedom, equality, justice, respect for human rights, tolerance and acceptance of differences as the near-universal values and said law and justice should be the same for all.

separated-powers.rationale: He praised Montesquieu's separation of powers, supported counter-powers through decentralisation and an independent audiovisual authority as a fourth power.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He said a political leader has the duty to refuse exclusion and asked for a minimum income for the victims of the new poverty.

party-controls-media.rationale: He said that before the 1982 law the State was sole master of the audiovisual media and used and abused it, and wanted an independent audiovisual authority written into the Constitution.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He wrote that Europe cannot conceive a common defence without the authority of a central political power, a task of long duration, and that the single market of 1992 must be built.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He said the President must be responsible for defence and external policy and that France's nuclear deterrent obeys the orders of the President of the Republic alone.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He said he would support a shorter presidential mandate only on condition that it be renewable only once.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He said France's loyalty to the Atlantic Alliance does not affect its autonomy and that solidarity among the Alliance's members must be confirmed.

death-penalty.rationale: He presented the abolition of the death penalty and of exceptional courts as a recent advance of the rule of law, which he called a fragile edifice.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: He defended the droit du sol, under which children born in France of foreign parents are French, asking why change what has served France well.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He announced that France cancelled a third of the debt owed by the poorest countries and urged easier terms, while also saying all debts incurred must be repaid and that cost can be cut without burdening taxpayers.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He told the UN that it is in the interest of the North to help the South, that levels of aid should be irreversible, and set France's 0.7 percent aid target.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He told the UN that France's deterrent force is independent, obeys the orders of the President alone, and is essential to its security and survival.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He said it is in the interest of democracy and France that the President elected by universal suffrage be both responsible and arbiter.

collective-defense.rationale: He told the Bundestag that the determination and solidarity of the members of the Atlantic Alliance must be clearly confirmed and that decoupling Europe from the American continent is dangerous.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He presented himself as President of all the French, arbiter and responsible for the nation's course, and wanted high officials not tied to a party.

elective-rulers.rationale: He said the President elected by universal suffrage should be responsible and arbiter, and attributed the weakness of the Fourth Republic to a President without powers.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: He defended the public pension system and retirement at sixty, accusing critics of hoping to hasten private insurance and saying pensions are not out of breath.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He spoke of the same alliance, the Atlantic Alliance, as the framework of French and German security and called its solidarity necessary, while keeping France outside the integrated command.

term-limits.rationale: He said he would support shortening the presidential term to five years provided it be renewable only once.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: He noted that Britain, Holland and Scandinavia let immigrants vote on local or national decisions and said he personally regretted that French mores do not allow it.

future-generations.rationale: He called for protection of the natural environment and for ethics of the third millennium so as to hand on a natural and genetically intact heritage to descendants.

arms-reduction.rationale: He called for a balance of armaments at a lower, sufficient and reasonable level, with verification, and for gradual reduction of forces.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He praised the 1982 Auroux laws that obliged companies to negotiate wages and working conditions every year, with employers' and workers' unions.

public-service-media.rationale: He wanted an audiovisual council with a minority of political nominees and a majority of professionals, outside direct or indirect political influence.

women-suffrage.rationale: He listed measures against discrimination of women at work among advances of rights and named the enslavement of women as an evil behind the principle that all are born free and equal in rights.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: He condemned a threat of exclusion by racial origins in the nationality-code debate and begged his readers to keep away the racist aberration.

conquest-no-lawful-claim.rationale: He said France has always refused to recognise the fait accompli and that Kuwait's sovereignty is not negotiable, any more than any other state's.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: He said it is painful but the law is the same for all that an immigrant who came illegally be turned back, to be applied humanely.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He asked for a minimum income so that a means of living is guaranteed to those who have nothing, as the condition of their reintegration.

notes: First audit. Primary texts: his three UN General Assembly addresses (1983, 1988, 1990) from the local UNGDC corpus, the Lettre à tous les Français (1988), his 1981 inauguration speech and his 1987 speech at the Panthéon, all from the Élysée archive of his speeches (fetched with the project's honest user agent). The 1983 Bundestag speech and the 1981 programme (110 propositions) were fetched but only partly searched. His record in office (laws signed) could not be reached on Légifrance or vie-publique, so record-based answers rest on his own accounts of it; see notFound. Themes searched in the Lettre: institutions, referendum and mandate, media, nationalisation and privatisation, decentralisation, social security, taxes and minimum income, unions, immigration and nationality, Europe, defence and nuclear arms, education, culture. Many statements remain null, so the uncertainty rule may fail.
